signature.one_line: Handheld skit: text colour boxed film subtitles, whip-pan character handoffs, silent captionless punchline.
unique_devices: Plain film subtitles only: small bold text colour Arial-style phrases with full punctuation on a faint translucent dark box at a fixed 66 % H; zero titles, graphics or b-roll
Whip-pan character handoffs: ~half of all cuts are whip pans and most cuts are J-leads, so the next line starts before the picture changes
Running gag: one short 2-word question repeated by every character, escalating toward a reveal
Silent payoff: the last ~17 % plays with no captions and no dialogue, and the grade shifts from warm beige to cool grey for the reveal
signature.why_it_works: Starts mid-scene with a name and a number, repetition builds the joke, and the wordless reveal lets the picture deliver the punchline.

hook.first_frame: Handheld medium shot of a seated person holding a phone in front of light-wood office shelves, mid-conversation; small text colour subtitle on a faint dark box at two-thirds height

structure.what: mid-conversation line naming a colleague and a big task with a number
first question and uncertain answer introduce the gag line; whip pan to the next person
escalation: next colleague repeats the uncertain answer; shot/reverse-shot
escalation 2: the responsible person is called in; whip pans between everyone
deflating one-word answer, decision to go and look
silent reveal of the unfinished space, deadpan reaction, captions off

captions.how: 1-5 words, one line, centred at 66 % H fixed for every shot; Inter 700 48 px text colour with a tight dark edge on a faint translucent black box; hard cut on the first word of each phrase

camera.what: handheld documentary coverage of each character

camera.how: slow handheld wides of the space, one deadpan close reaction

transitions.how: horizontal motion-blur whip ~6-8 frames; next line leads the cut (J-cut on most cuts)

case.caption: sentence case as written dialogue (capital on sentence starts and names)

captions_spec.punctuation: full: commas, full stops and question marks kept

grouping.sync: phrase-level, cut on the first word of each phrase
grouping.break: at punctuation / natural pauses; previous phrase hard-cuts to the next

layout.rule: fixed position for every shot (does not follow the speaker)

closest_match.google: Inter Bold (or Arimo Bold for a closer Arial look)

caption.letterform_evidence: Arial-like: double-storey a, angled terminals on t and ?, tall I without serifs, compact widths
caption.calibration_note: measured phrases (source text withheld): a 2-word phrase with digits at 2.27 % H / 22.4 % W over a dark T-shirt; a 2-word question with a capital I at 1.8 % H / 15.1 % W over a light wall (yellow-only ink)
caption.stroke: thin dark outline / tight shadow ~1.5 px @1080, e.g. text-shadow 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,.8) (estimated)
caption.box: translucent black rectangle behind the line: rgba(0,0,0,.25), radius ~4 px @1080 (estimated), padding ~13 px left/right and ~12 px top/bottom @1080; a short phrase box spans ~x 41-59 %, y 64.4-67.5 % (3.0 % H)

animation.entry: hard cut on the first word of the phrase (within ~1 frame)
animation.exit: hard cut when the next phrase starts (or stays until the shot changes)

other_text_spec.text: none; the payoff (last ~17 % of runtime) plays with no captions

style.look_intent: soft, low-to-mid contrast, muted warm beige office; the reveal switches to cooler, darker grey

sound.music: music bed likely (low under dialogue, gaps ~8 dB below speech); light ambience carries the silent reveal

sound.method: heuristic (onset-envelope beat periodicity + level in speech gaps); not a classifier

catalog_styles.name: Minimal Subtitle Style
catalog_styles.role: yellow film subtitles on a faint box

catalog_styles.name: Dialogue-First Interview Edit
catalog_styles.role: J-leads: next line starts before the cut

use_when: A scripted multi-person skit or scene shot handheld in a real location
The joke builds on a repeated line handed from character to character
The ending can be shown rather than said (a visual reveal)
The brand wants a native, unpolished look with captions only for accessibility
avoid_when: Single-speaker talking-head or educational content that needs emphasis captions and graphics
No room for a silent ending (the payoff needs the last ~15-20 % of runtime as pure picture)
brand_prompt:
Use /video-pipeline with /video-captions on videos/<project>. Apply style blueprint B21 (video-reference-match/references/blueprints/B21.json) to this brand.
Canvas 1080x1920, 30 fps. Multi-character handheld scene.

BRAND TOKENS (use the brand's colour/font for each role; keep the contrast relationship: subtitle {{TEXT}} must stay >= 4.5:1 against its box over both light walls and dark clothing)
- {{TEXT}}: default #F2C911 (subtitle yellow)
- {{ACCENT}}: default #F2C911 (same as text; no separate emphasis)
- {{ACCENT_2}}: none
- {{SURFACE}}: default rgba(0,0,0,.25) (subtitle box)
- {{CARD_BG}}: none
- {{FONT_DISPLAY}}: none (no titles)
- {{FONT_BODY}}: default Inter 700 (Arimo Bold for an Arial look)
- {{HANDLE}}: not on screen
- {{LOGO}}: none (the skit carries no branding on screen)

CAPTIONS
1. Latin, as spoken, sentence case like written dialogue; keep commas, full stops and question marks; no emoji.
2. 1-5 words per subtitle (a clause), one line, break at punctuation or natural pauses.
3. {{FONT_BODY}} at 48 px, {{TEXT}}, tracking 0, tight dark edge (text-shadow 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,.8)), on a {{SURFACE}} rectangle, radius ~4 px, padding ~13 px left/right and ~12 px top/bottom; the box hugs the line (~3 % H tall).
4. Centred, centre y 66 % H, the same position on every shot (does not follow the speaker).
5. Hard cut in on the first word of each phrase (within ~1 frame), hard cut out on the next phrase; no idle motion.
6. Turn captions OFF for the silent payoff (last ~17 % of runtime).

EDIT DEVICES
7. Open mid-conversation: first word inside ~4 frames, a name/role and a concrete number in the first line; no title card.
8. Handoffs between characters: ~half the cuts are horizontal whip pans (~6-8 frames motion blur); on most cuts start the next line before the picture changes (J-cut).
9. Median shot ~3 s; no punch-ins, no titles, no graphics, no b-roll.
10. Payoff: the last ~17 % of runtime as wordless wide reveal shots plus one deadpan reaction; grade the reveal cooler and darker than the rest.

GRADE: Grade from the user's footage (video-style / grade.py); target look: soft, muted warm beige interiors, then a cooler grey reveal.
SOUND: quiet bed or room tone under dialogue (gaps ~8 dB below speech), ambience through the reveal; -14 LUFS, true peak <= -1 dBTP.
